descriptionChirho: To physically leave a place or person behind, abandon, or forsake; Arabic consistently uses taraka (تَرَكَ), Korean uses beorida/tteonada (버리다/떠나다), Swahili uses -acha, Hindi uses chhodna (छोड़ना). Covers all tenses and persons of the active 'leave/depart' meaning.

Passive of the 'leave' sense: to be left behind, be abandoned, remain; Arabic uses the passive yutraku (يُترَكُ), Korean uses beoryeojida (버려지다) or namgyeojida (남겨지다), Swahili uses -achwa. Distinct from passive forgiveness.

To forgive sins or cancel debts; Arabic consistently uses ghafara (غَفَرَ/يَغفِرُ) or a'faa (أَعْفَى for debt remission), Korean uses yongseo-hada (용서하다) or tanggam-hada (탕감하다 for debt), Swahili uses -samehe, Hindi uses kshama karna (क्षमा करना). The debt-cancellation and sin-forgiveness uses share the same Greek sense.

Passive of the 'forgive' sense: sins or debts are forgiven or cancelled; Arabic uses passive ghufират/yughfaru (غُفِرَت/يُغفَرُ), Korean uses yongseo-batda (용서받다) or saham-batda (사함받다), Swahili uses -samehewa. Clearly distinct from passive 'be left' by Arabic root and all target-language glosses.

To permit, allow, or let someone do something; Arabic uses samaha (سَمَحَ) or da'a (دَعَ/يَدَعُ), Korean uses heorak-hada (허락하다), Swahili uses -ruhusu, Hindi uses aagya dena (आज्ञा देना) or rahne dena (रहने देना). Includes indicative statements of permitting and imperatives meaning 'let/allow/leave alone' where the sense is non-interference rather than physical departure.

To send away or dismiss a person, particularly in the context of divorce (let him/her send away a spouse); Spanish uses despida, Arabic uses yatruk (يَتْرُكْ) in jussive, Korean uses beorira (버리라), Swahili uses asimwache. Distinguished from simple 'leave' by the causative/permissive framing (sending someone else away).

To release or yield up, as in yielding up one's spirit at death (Matt 27:50); Arabic uses aslama (أَسْلَمَ, to hand over/surrender), Korean uses noh-atda (놓았다), Swahili uses -toa (give out/emit), Spanish uses entregar (hand over). Semantically distinct from 'leave' or 'permit' — this is a deliberate releasing or giving forth.

To neglect or leave undone important duties; English 'neglect', Spanish 'descuidar/descuidasteis', Hindi chhodna (छोड़ना) in the sense of abandoning responsibilities, Arabic taraka (تَرَكتُم). Distinguished from physical 'leave' by the object being duties or commandments rather than places or persons.
